evals.name: pwa-update-waits-for-tabs

evals.expected_output: Explains that the new worker waits while any tab uses the old one, and that reloading doesn't help. Finds registerType 'prompt' with no onNeedRefresh / registration.waiting handling (code.sw-update-flow warn, file:line), notes navigations come from the precached shell (code.sw-html-cache-first), and recommends a prompt-then-reload flow instead of switching to autoUpdate/skipWaiting. Links Question 7.
expectations: Says yes, it's expected: the new service worker waits until no tab uses the old one, and reloading doesn't hand over control

If it mentions autoUpdate/skipWaiting, warns that taking over immediately can break pages still running old code
Notes that navigations are served from the precached index.html (navigateFallback), so HTTP headers don't decide HTML freshness
Links to the article section for service workers (#question-7-...)
Leaves the repo unmodified

evals.name: real-site-astro-workers
evals.prompt: before I publish the next post, can you check that ihabkhattab.com won't serve people stale pages after a deploy? repo is ~/Workspace/personal-website
evals.expected_output: Runs the CLI against https://ihabkhattab.com/ and reads the repo. Confirms that /_astro/* is served one-year immutable and that public/_headers sets it. Probes a missing /_astro/ URL and reports that the 404 also gets the one-year immutable header. For the HTML's missing ETag, reads src/worker.ts, sees that it copies headers through (line 15), and points to Cloudflare's HTML-rewriting zone features (Email Obfuscation and similar) as dashboard settings to check, without claiming which one is on. Treats the Cloudflare HIT without Age as info. Notes there's no service worker on the site itself, and doesn't edit files.
expectations: Checked the live site (ran the CLI or fetched headers) and reports the headers it actually saw
Answers the question directly: HTML is revalidated on every use (max-age=0, must-revalidate), so a deploy reaches browsers on their next visit
Confirms that hashed /_astro/* files are served public, max-age=31536000, immutable and that public/_headers sets it, so config and live headers agree

Reports that a missing /_astro/ file returns 404 with the same one-year immutable header (the public/_headers rule also matches misses), so a browser that requests a new hash too early keeps the 404 for a year
Reports the HTML's missing ETag without claiming src/worker.ts drops it (the Worker copies headers through)
Treats Cloudflare's cache HIT on HTML as not a stale-page risk (Worker cache is per-version / no Age), rather than telling the user to purge or remove a rule
Doesn't report a real service worker on the site (the only register() call is a code sample in a blog post)
Leaves the personal-website repo unmodified (git status clean)
Opens with a direct answer to the user's question (cause or verdict) in the first two sentences
Backs the main conclusion with a test (a reproduction, a build in a scratch copy, or a live request), or says why it couldn't

evals.name: ci-check-vite-s3
evals.prompt: can you add a step to our deploy workflow that fails the build when a deploy could leave users stuck on an old version? prod is https://admin.acme.example/
evals.expected_output: Adds a step after the S3 upload and CloudFront invalidation in .github/workflows/deploy.yml that checks the prod URL with the ikhattab/stale-deploy-check action (or a pinned CLI that keeps each report between runs and passes the previous one as --baseline). Warns that with today's `aws s3 sync --delete` the new step will fail from the second deploy (assets.previous-removed), and that `max-age=3600` on index.html fails html.max-age, so the user knows the step will go red until those are fixed. Doesn't turn on --strict without asking.
expectations: Edits .github/workflows/deploy.yml, adding the check after the upload and invalidation steps, not before
Checks the production URL with a pinned version: the ikhattab/stale-deploy-check action at a version tag, or the CLI as stale-deploy-check@<major>.<minor> or an exact version
Compares each deploy with the previous one: the action (which does this by default), or keeping each report (cache, artifact, or bucket) and passing the previous one with --baseline
Keeps the report even when the check fails, so the next run still has a baseline: the action does this, or a save step with if: always() or equivalent
Warns that aws s3 sync --delete will make the check fail from the second deploy on, because the old chunks are deleted, and names the fix
Warns that --cache-control 'public, max-age=3600' applies to index.html, so the check will fail on the HTML's lifetime until that changes
Doesn't add --strict without asking
Says the live check couldn't run from here if the URL is unreachable, rather than implying it passed
Changes only the workflow file
